diagnosis: kernel_lrat_chain aborted with 'LRAT chain cites a literal with no unit id'. Root cause: propagate_service gated the LRAT root-unit sweep on the SOLVER's level (`if (lrat && k.level == 0)`) while emit_root_units already applies the correct PER-LITERAL test (`a.level != 0` -> continue). A propagation-forced literal is stamped at its TRUE level (D-LEVEL-2, kernel_assign_ref/kernel_assign_binary take the max level among the reason's other literals, starting at 0), so a clause whose other literals are all root-false forces a literal at level 0 WHILE THE SOLVER STANDS HIGHER. Those literals were skipped by the sweep and kept unit_ids[v] == 0; since 0 is LRAT's line terminator, any later DIRECT citation of unit_ids (emit_root_units itself, analyze, strengthen, substitute, bve) emitted a TRUNCATED antecedent list rather than a wrong one, which every LRAT checker rejects. Reason-walk chains are structurally immune -- kernel_reason_walk only reads unit_ids under `reason == UNIT_REASON`, otherwise citing the reason clause and recursing -- which is why the defect survived so long and why a first reproduction attempt came back green. LATENT UNTIL 2026-08-04: pre-chrono the true level always equalled the current level at a propagation fixpoint, and pre-TB4b a learned unit backjumped to level 0 before propagating; TB4b's unit chrono routing (e404668) asserts a learned unit at level 0 while standing higher (14,088 of 18,635 conflicts on veer_axi), which is what made this reachable. INVISIBLE TO DRAT, which re-derives units itself -- so every tier run and every DRAT fuzz leg was blind, and the shipped LRAT legs were vacuous on this path because fuzz CNFs are ~90 vars while the routing needs level-1 > chrono_levels (100). Fixed 2026-08-04: drop the `k.level == 0` conjunct in propagate_service, and assert in kernel_lrat_chain that no antecedent id is 0 (a permanent guard in the family of Proof::add_rup's no-tautology / no-empty-chain asserts, L13). Demonstrated by a paired debug fuzz leg with chrono forced: unfixed 36 assert-aborts before the max-failures cap (~2,600 cases), fixed 0 failures in 10,000.
